title: U.S. House · Michigan's 2nd District
area: Michigan's 2nd Congressional District — the northwestern Lower Peninsula, including Midland and parts of the Grand Traverse region.

context.text: Cook Political Report rated Michigan's 2nd District R+15 for the 2026 cycle. Donald Trump won the district 64.3%–34.2% in 2024.
Incumbent John Moolenaar was unopposed in the August 4, 2026 Republican primary. Ben Ambrose defeated Jamie Hill and Clyde Welford in the Democratic primary with 44.3% of the vote.

candidates.name: John Moolenaar
candidates.ballotNote: Unopposed in the August 4, 2026 Republican primary

summary.text: Moolenaar is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Michigan's 2nd District, first elected in 2014. A chemist by training, he worked in business and education administration and served on the Midland City Council, in the Michigan House and in the Michigan Senate before Congress. He sits on the House Appropriations Committee and chairs the House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party.

background.text: Born in Midland, Michigan, in 1961.
Earned a bachelor's degree in chemistry from Hope College (1983) and a master's degree in public administration from Harvard University (1989).

According to his official biography, he began his career as a chemist, then worked in business development and as a school administrator. Ballotpedia lists employment with Dow Chemical and a role as director of the Small Business Center for the Middle Michigan Development Corporation.
Served on the Midland City Council from 1997 to 2000.
Served in the Michigan House of Representatives from 2003 to 2008 and in the Michigan Senate from 2011 to 2014.
Elected to the U.S. House in 2014 and took office in 2015, representing the 4th District until the 2022 redistricting and the 2nd District since 2023.

Serves on the House Appropriations Committee, where his official biography says he is Michigan's only member; his 2025-2026 subcommittee assignments are Agriculture; Labor, Health and Human Services, Education; and National Security, Department of State.

Chairs the House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party and is a member of the Congressional School Choice Caucus, according to his official biography.
According to his official biography, he and his wife, Amy, raised their family in Michigan and have six children and four grandchildren.
Ran unopposed in the August 4, 2026 Republican primary.

priorities.text: Says he strongly supports the Great Lakes Restoration Initiative and will keep working across the aisle to secure funding for it.
priorities.quote: I strongly support the Great Lakes Restoration Initiative (GLRI). Since the initiative was launched in 2010, GLRI funds have been used to support over 3,000 restoration projects to improve water quality, protect and restore native habitat, fight invasive species, and prevent beach closings.

priorities.text: Prioritizes building a replacement for the Soo Locks, describing an unscheduled closure as a threat to the North American industrial economy.
Says Congress must reduce federal spending and the national debt, and supports reforms to Social Security and Medicare that would not affect current retirees or those nearing retirement.

positions.summary: In a January 2026 press release he opposed extending the enhanced ACA premium tax credits, calling the extension wrong and saying it would increase health care costs.
positions.quote: Extending a COVID-era subsidy for those making more than 400 percent of the poverty level is wrong and will only increase health care costs.

record.text: In the 119th Congress (2025–2026), chairs the House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party and serves on the House Committee on Appropriations (Agriculture, Rural Development, FDA and Related Agencies; Labor, HHS, Education; National Security, Department of State and Related Programs subcommittees).

candidates.name: Ben Ambrose
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary with 44.3% of the vote

summary.text: Ambrose is a 20-year U.S. Marine Corps infantry veteran from Hesperia, Michigan, and the Democratic nominee for Michigan's 2nd District. After his military service he worked as a federal employee for Oregon Sen. Ron Wyden, and he describes his campaign as a return to public service.

background.text: Grew up in Hesperia, Michigan; WCMU also describes him as a Hesperia native.

Served in the U.S. Marine Corps for 20 years as an infantryman. In a 9&10 News candidate questionnaire he said he enlisted six days after high school graduation and deployed to Iraq and Afghanistan, with humanitarian missions to Haiti and Marine Expeditionary Unit deployments.

After his military career he worked as a federal employee for Oregon Democratic Sen. Ron Wyden, according to WCMU. In the 9&10 questionnaire he said he testified before the Senate Veterans' Affairs Committee about cuts by the Department of Government Efficiency, which he said led him to run.
Won the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary with 44.3% of the vote, ahead of Jamie Hill (42.3%) and Clyde Welford (13.4%).

priorities.text: Lowering the cost of essentials by holding large corporations accountable for price gouging.
priorities.quote: Bringing down the cost of essentials like groceries and gas by holding big corporations accountable for unfair price gouging

priorities.text: Increasing federal funding for public schools and making college more affordable.
priorities.quote: Increase federal funding for public schools and reduce class sizes
Champion Medicare for All to guarantee quality healthcare for every American

positions.summary: Campaign website says he supports Medicare for All and lists protecting and strengthening the Affordable Care Act.
positions.quote: Ben proudly supports Medicare for All and is committed to making affordable, accessible healthcare a reality for every American.

positions.summary: Campaign website lists transitioning to clean energy sources and reducing carbon emissions among his priorities.
positions.quote: Transition to clean energy sources and reduce carbon emissions

candidates.researchNotes: Campaign website (ambrose4congress.com) priorities page read in full. Healthcare and climate positions already cited. No campaign statements found taking a side on other guide issues (abortion: the site says only 'Ensure women have access to reproductive healthcare', not recorded as an abortion stance).

candidates.name: Charlotte Magoon

summary.text: Magoon is the Green Party nominee for Michigan's 2nd District. A registered nurse, she describes herself as a longtime Kent County resident who attended college as a single mother.

background.text: In her Ballotpedia survey she says she has lived in Kent County most of her life and attended college as a single mother.
Earned a nursing degree (BSN) from Grand Valley State University in 2009, according to her Ballotpedia survey.

Says she has worked as a nurse for 17 years in inpatient acute care, rehabilitation, long-term care and now community hospice; before nursing she says she worked in food service and as a factory worker and ran a home daycare.

priorities.text: Not depending on corporate or PAC money.
priorities.quote: The Green Party does not depend on corporations or Supper PACs and I will never accept donations intended to pressure me to vote against my conscience.

priorities.text: Wages and taxes on the wealthy.
priorities.quote: We must hold corporations accountable to pay a living wage. We must demand that the rich pay their fair share in taxes

priorities.text: Fairer media coverage of minor parties and independent candidates.
priorities.quote: Americans have the right to know and hear from all candidates, not just the 2 that have the most money to spend on their campaigns.

candidates.name: Richard Sills

summary.text: Sills is the Natural Law Party nominee for Michigan's 2nd District. According to Ballotpedia, he has worked in meat processing, printing and marketing and farming.

background.text: A native of the Cincinnati area who moved to Michigan in 1983, according to Ballotpedia.
Worked in the meat-packing industry and owned two meat processing plants in Michigan; Ballotpedia says he was involved in implementing a federal safety-standards program for the industry.
Also worked in the printing and marketing industries and, when he entered the 2018 election, was an ostrich farmer.
